name: nothing-to-scan
description: Four export rows that all look scannable and none of which are, each covering a shape the runZero export really produces. Row 1 has an in-policy 10/8 address but last_agent_id null -- nulls.UUID marshals to JSON null, not to an empty string, so the guard has to treat None as missing; there is no Explorer to run the scan on. Row 2 is 100.64/10 CGNAT: the near-miss that matters now that ALLOW_LIST names all three RFC1918 ranges (10/8, 172.16/12, 192.168/16), because anything that widened the check to 'anything private-looking' would start scanning it. Row 3 is a routable public address, the case where a wrong answer means scanning someone else's network from a customer Explorer. Row 4 is IPv6-only, which reaches ip_address() and must be rejected on version rather than fed to the IPv4-only ip_to_int() -- that path splits on dots and would abort the whole run on a colon-separated address, taking the other Explorers' scans down with it. The run must therefore make exactly ONE request and then stop: no scan, and no bulk delete, because deleting assets that were never scanned destroys the only record that they exist.

routes.name: passive asset export, nothing in policy
